title: observer adapter: tmux and ps probes run without a context and can wedge the watcher; decodeEvents is dead
summary: Found by comment-reduction batch 18 (2026-09-26) and reported without changing code. (1) realTmuxRunner and realPSRunner call exec.Command without a context from the Watch goroutine. A wedged tmux server (the ADR-0063 hang) or a hung ps blocks the watcher, which ends in the 'watcher leaked' case. (2) decodeEvents has no callers and is kept alive by `var _ = decodeEvents`. It duplicates parseEvents but fails where parseEvents skips bad lines. (3) The test helpers repeat each other: syncSink and syncBuffer are the same buffer, and amplFakeCloser and countingCloser are the same closer. (4) core_adapter_channel_test.go ignores os.WriteFile errors on lines 17 and 31. (5) TestCoreAdapter_HasNoStderrLinesAndNoEnvReads does not catch os.LookupEnv or os.Environ. (6) The stall reason always says 'no stdout growth', even when workspace activity is also watched.
fix: Pass a context with a deadline to every probe exec (exec.CommandContext), bounded by config. Delete decodeEvents. Merge the duplicate helpers. Check the WriteFile errors. Widen the env-read pin. Make the stall reason name what was actually watched.
acceptance: A probe that hangs past its deadline returns and the watcher keeps running (test with a blocking fake)
priority_rationale: inbox review 2026-09-27: Latent: a wedged tmux server stalls the bridge itself first, and the leak arm limits the observer's damage to one goroutine and fd per phase.
